For not even they who receive circumcision do themselves keep the Law; but they desire to have you circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh." Here he shows that they suffered this, not willingly but of necessity, and affords them an opportunity of retreat, almost speaking in their defence, and exhorting them to abandon their teachers with all speed.
13: Argues the legalists pushed circumcision to look impressive outwardly and to avoid persecution for the cross, boasting in the Galatians' compliance.

For neither do those who are circumcised, these, keep the Law; but they wish you to be circumcised, that they may glory in your flesh. Because of the weakness of the flesh, he says, the Law cannot be fulfilled. Hence the Jews too keep the precepts and doctrines of men rather than the commandments of God, doing neither the bodily Law (for that indeed is impossible) nor the spiritual Law, which they do not understand.
14: Says Paul boasted only in Christ's crucifixion, which he saw as ending his ties to the world, and that outward circumcision means nothing compared to becoming a new creation.

For as it was in the days of Noah, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For as they were in the days before the flood, eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until Noah entered into the ark, and they knew not until the flood came and took them all away, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
15: Says Paul boasted only in Christ's crucifixion, which he saw as ending his ties to the world, and that outward circumcision means nothing compared to becoming a new creation.

"For neither is circumcision any thing, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature. And as many as shall walk by this rule, peace be upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God." Observe the power of the Cross, to what a pitch it hath raised him! not only hath it put to death for him all mundane affairs, but hath set him far above the Old Dispensation. What can be comparable to this power?
16: Notes Paul pronounces peace and mercy on those living by the measuring standard of God's truth, identifying them as the true Israel of God.
A blessing on those who walk in God's truth

And whoever follow this rule, peace upon them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God. All things are directed by a norm; and whether they are crooked or straight is shown up once the rule has been laid against them. So too the teaching of God is, as it were, a kind of norm of speech, which judges between what is righteous and what is unrighteous: whoever follows it will have in himself the peace which surpasses all understanding; and after peace, mercy, which is preeminent in the Israel of God.

"From henceforth let no man trouble me." This he says not as though he were wearied or overpowered; he who chose to do and suffer all for his disciples' sake; he who said, "Be instant in season, out of season;" (2 Tim. iv: 2.) he who said, "If peradventure God may give them repentance unto the knowledge of the truth, and they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil;" (2 Tim. ii: 25, 26.) how shall he now become relaxed and fall back? Wherefore does he say this?

The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brothers. Amen. Not dissension, not slavery of the Law, not quarreling, not wrangling, but the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. By no means with the flesh, by no means with the soul; either because, having been made spiritual, you cease to be flesh and soul, or because in the principal part those things too that are lesser are comprehended. For the soul and the flesh are subject to the spirit.
